title: LumenEx KV cache weekly sync - prefetch & reuse debrief
summary: Weekly POC check-in reviewing KV/prefix cache hit rates and a proposed prefetch/eviction adjustment. We validated a small latency improvement for high-frequency prefixes but saw increased memory pressure; agreed to test a targeted prefetch window and tighter eviction rules before next sync.
action_items: Marco Rivera - share filtered KV hit-rate CSV (by prefix bucket) and the quick Python filter script - 2026-05-25
Sofia Chen - run a 24h microbenchmark with prefetch window=128 tokens on staging and post results to shared sheet - 2026-05-26
Aisha Patel - email security package and SOC2 snapshot, plus orchestration notes for VPC demo - 2026-05-24
Rajiv Malhotra - validate memory headroom on dedicated node type (g5.12x) and report OOM risk - 2026-05-27
Grace Park - consolidate success criteria for pilot (latency p95 target, cost per 1k calls, hit-rate target) - 2026-05-28
next_steps: Run targeted prefetch experiment (prefetch window 64/128) on 2nd staging cluster
Share detailed hit-rate per prefix and per-route breakdown
Map outage/slow patterns to eviction events using trace IDs and forward to Marco
Schedule on-prem demo next Tuesday if memory looks good
Redwood to propose tightened eviction rule (age+LRU hybrid) for high-cardinality routes
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-22 15:00 PDT | Duration: 43m | Attendees: Aisha, Marco - Redwood; Sofia, Rajiv, Grace - LumenEx

Summary: quick check-in on KV/prefix cache pilot, results from last 72h, and action items. Audio transcription medium quality, some names and terms may be slightly off.

[00:00] Aisha Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, you all good timewise?
[00:05] Sofia Chen: yeah we're good, just juggling a deploy so might be a little jumpy, sorry in advance
[00:08] Aisha Patel: no worries, we'll run through the metrics first, then tuning recs, then next steps
[00:15] Marco Rivera: hi team, Marco here, SE on the cache side. i pulled the last 72 hours of KV hits—overall hit-rate's up 9% since we enabled prefix indexing but it's uneven by route
[00:28] Rajiv Malhotra: can you clarify "prefix indexing" again, we call it prefetch in our notes so i want to align the terms
[00:33] Marco Rivera: sure, sorry, different words. by prefix indexing i mean the early-key prefix fingerprinting we discussed, plus the prefetch window where we prime the KV with likely continuations
[00:43] Grace Park: ok makes sense. so what's the hit-rate split? global vs top-10 prefixes?
[00:48] Marco Rivera: global hit-rate around 37% average; top-10 prefixes are about 68% hit, but tail prefixes drop below 10% — we see a long tail effect
[01:02] Sofia Chen: that matches what we thought. some of our chat flows spawn very unique prefixes per user, so it's noisy
[01:08] Marco Rivera: exactly, the reuse is great for templated prompts and product description routes but much worse for freeform search style prompts
[01:18] Aisha Patel: did you notice latency improvements on the higher hit routes?
[01:22] Marco Rivera: yes, p50 improved by ~8ms and p95 improved by ~46ms on top-10 prefixes, but when we enabled aggressive prefetch across many prefixes memory usage spiked and caused queueing on the NVMe spillover path
[01:36] Rajiv Malhotra: that NVMe spillover—i need to be clear on the eviction behavior. are refcounts used or pure LRU?
[01:42] Marco Rivera: right now it's LRU with a small age threshold. we do have an experiment candidate: hybrid LRU+age where very old prefixes are evicted earlier, plus an optional size cap per prefix bucket
[01:56] Grace Park: hybrid sounds interesting. what's the ops cost of monitoring that?
[02:00] Marco Rivera: negligible to instrument; it's mostly config changes. we'll add per-bucket metrics to the dashboard so you can see eviction rates per route
[02:10] Sofia Chen: can we get the per-route hit-rate CSV? that's easiest for our analysts
[02:13] Marco Rivera: yes, i'll export and share the filtered CSV and the python script i used to bucket prefixes
[02:18] Aisha Patel: noted. quick question on prefetch window sizing — we recommended 64 tokens initially, you tried 256 in staging last week?
[02:26] Sofia Chen: we tried 256 because we thought longer continuations would help, but memory blowup happened after 36 hours
[02:31] Marco Rivera: that's consistent. 256 is aggressive for your workload; the sweet spot might be 64 or 128 based on the distribution Sofia shared earlier
[02:39] Rajiv Malhotra: so if we go to 64, do we expect a big drop in hit-rate?
[02:44] Marco Rivera: possibly a small one, maybe 3-5% global hit-rate delta, but memory usage comes way down and tail latency stabilizes
[02:50] Grace Park: that would be acceptable if p95 latency stays under our 650ms goal
[02:55] Aisha Patel: I want to call out cost tradeoffs — higher prefetch = more tokens cached = more GPU memory + slightly higher token processing. we should map that to cost per 1k calls in the pilot metrics
[03:06] Sofia Chen: yes please, that cost per 1k will help product decide; can Redwood model that for us?
[03:10] Marco Rivera: we can approximate with current token counts and memory pricing; i'll add a simple model to the sheet
[03:16] Rajiv Malhotra: security question — if we prefetch more, is any PII persisted in the cache? our policy forbids storing PII beyond X days
[03:23] Aisha Patel: good catch. by default KV cache is encrypted at rest and we support KMS, but we can add filters to not cache certain routes or to redact tokens before caching
[03:32] Grace Park: could we do redaction on the fly? that might affect hit-rate though
[03:36] Marco Rivera: redaction reduces hit-rate because it modifies the keys; we often recommend route-level exclusion for high-PII flows and redaction for lower-risk ones
[03:45] Sofia Chen: for the search route we can likely exclude, for templated the redaction might be ok
[03:50] Rajiv Malhotra: action item for me to map which routes have PII risk
[03:54] Aisha Patel: perfect.
[03:55] [04:00] Aisha Patel: okay let's go through the benchmark notes — Sofia, you ran a 72-hour run with prefetch=256 and prefetch=64 on different clusters?
[04:07] Sofia Chen: yep, we split traffic by route. the 256 cluster averaged 41% hit early then dropped to 33% after two days when memory pressure triggered eviction bursts
[04:18] Marco Rivera: those eviction bursts correspond to a spike in latency as the runtime swapped to disk. i saw spikes in p99 during those times
[04:24] Grace Park: do we have trace IDs for those spikes? we want to map to user sessions if possible
[04:29] Marco Rivera: yes, we can correlate — i'll forward the trace id list in the CSV export
[04:35] Aisha Patel: what's the recommended next tuning step? Marco?
[04:38] Marco Rivera: three things — reduce prefetch to 64 for the global experiment, introduce per-prefix bucket size caps for high-cardinality routes, and flip on hybrid LRU+age eviction for the staging cluster
[04:47] Sofia Chen: sounds reasonable. how do we pick the bucket caps?
[04:50] Marco Rivera: bucket caps set as percentiles: hold top-10 prefixes up to X MB each, tail prefixes get much smaller caps. i can propose initial numbers based on today's distribution
[04:59] Rajiv Malhotra: any risks to dedicated capacity if we push this to Dedicated Redwood nodes?
[05:04] Marco Rivera: Dedicated reduces noisy neighbor risk and gives predictable headroom; memory pressure still matters but you can pick larger instance types. downside is higher committed cost
[05:13] Grace Park: product question — if Dedicated brings predictability, would the rollout be faster?
[05:16] Aisha Patel: typically yes — Dedicated with pinned model variants reduces fallback complexity. but you'd need procurement signoff and capacity reservation
[05:23] Sofia Chen: procurement is fine if we have clear success metrics; Grace will finalize those by next week
[05:28] Grace Park: yes i'll post those after this call
[05:31] Marco Rivera: one more operational note: we saw a small bug where prefix canonicalization differed across model versions, which caused key duplication. that's been patched in the runtime but we recommend pinning model version during the pilot window
[05:45] Rajiv Malhotra: pinning is fine, i'll coordinate with infra to lock versions on staging
[05:50] Aisha Patel: security pack — we'll send SOC2 summary and the KMS integration guide. Rajiv, is there a specific KMS you use?
[05:58] Rajiv Malhotra: we use HashiCorp Vault for dev, cloud KMS in prod — we'll need both notes
[06:03] Marco Rivera: we support both; I'll include HCV notes about token rotation and the S3 encrypted snapshots behavior
[06:10] Sofia Chen: curious about the dashboard — can we get per-route latency and eviction overlays?
[06:14] Marco Rivera: yes, we'll add an eviction overlay and an event stream for eviction spikes; should make debugging easier
[06:20] Grace Park: for acceptance criteria, i'd like p95 < 650ms on core flows, hit-rate > 45% for templated routes, and cost per 1k calls reduced vs baseline
[06:30] Aisha Patel: we'll capture that. quick question — competitors? did you evaluate any other approaches?
[06:34] Grace Park: we put together a short list, included OpenAI managed caching ideas and a Cohere memcache experiment; both looked heavier operationally than Redwood's runtime for our constraints
[06:45] Marco Rivera: ok noted.
[06:47] [07:00] Aisha Patel: ok let's do a quick recap and owners
[07:02] Marco Rivera: i'll share the CSV, the bucket script, and a proposed eviction config - due 5/25
[07:10] Sofia Chen: i'll run prefetch=64 24h microbench and upload results - due 5/26
[07:15] Rajiv Malhotra: i'll validate memory headroom and confirm dedicated node sizing - due 5/27
[07:20] Grace Park: finalize success criteria and post to the sheet - due 5/28
[07:24] Aisha Patel: i'll send SOC2 + KMS notes and propose next meeting time - due 5/24
[07:31] Sofia Chen: one quick question — if we switch to hybrid eviction will it cause more misses initially because keys are evicted more aggressively?
[07:37] Marco Rivera: short term maybe, but the idea is to reduce noisy long-tail occupancy so overall hit-rate on important prefixes should improve
[07:45] Rajiv Malhotra: last ops question — can we simulate OOM locally? we want to test prefetch failures without hitting prod disks
[07:51] Marco Rivera: yes, we have an OOM test harness; i'll give steps in the export doc
[07:56] Grace Park: sounds good. thanks everybody, this was productive
[08:00] Aisha Patel: thanks all, we'll follow up with the artifacts. next sync same time next week unless we need an extra slot for the on-prem demo

End of transcript.
